A1.justification: Both PDFs describe iLRM. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching material moved between the main text and appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments on RE10K, DL3DV, and ACID, with quantitative results, qualitative comparisons, architectural ablations, and resource measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds wide-coverage DL3DV comparisons and further architectural ablations.

M1.justification: The core tokenization, attention updates, token uplifting, Gaussian decoder, and training objective remain unchanged. v2 adds an optional reconstruction procedure involving per-scene fine-tuning of generated Gaussians, evaluated as Ours10 and Ours50 in Table 5.

E1.justification: The dataset families remain RE10K, ACID, and DL3DV, but v2 adds full-sequence, wide-coverage DL3DV reconstruction using 16 or 32 input views over approximately 350 frames. This substantially extends scene-coverage conditions beyond the retained 50-frame and 100-frame evaluations, rather than merely increasing views within their existing ranges.

E2.justification: v2 Table 5 adds evaluated comparisons against LongLRM, optimization-based 3D-GS, and Mip-Splatting, including fine-tuned LongLRM. These were not evaluated comparators in v1. The previous feed-forward comparator set remains represented.

E3.justification: The new wide-coverage protocol reserves every eighth frame for testing, selects inputs through camera-position/direction clustering, and introduces a resolution curriculum and optimization/fine-tuning budgets. Existing high-resolution Table 4 changes resource measurements from H100 to RTX 4090, with H100 fallback for DepthSplat. These hardware-dependent measurements are not directly comparable across versions.

E4.justification: v2 adds ablations testing repeated image injection and resolution decoupling in Table 8, plus random versus low-resolution-feature initialization in Appendix E/Table 9. The earlier self-attention and group-attention ablations are retained there. Conversely, v1's runtime/memory sweep over 2–256 views is removed, and the equal-Gaussian experiment loses its four-GPU training case.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, evaluation seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The initialization standard deviation describes model initialization, not uncertainty in experimental results.

E6.justification: Many reported scores change: RE10K two-view PSNR changes from 28.17 to 28.65, while 24-view DL3DV PSNR changes from 27.97 to 27.38. v2 adds DepthSplat results at 11 and 24 views, wide-coverage results, and new ablation outcomes. It removes the runtime sweep and four-GPU result. These are reported result revisions; the PDFs do not establish a single cause for the changes.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, attention equations, loss definition, and appendix FLOPs calculation are retained. Neither version contains additional theorems or proofs, and the new ablation interpretations introduce no formal mathematical development.

C1.justification: The three central design contributions and conclusion remain stable. v2's introduction adds a claim of outperforming optimization-based 3D-GS approaches in wide-coverage reconstruction with approximately 0.5-second inference, extending the earlier emphasis on superiority over feed-forward methods.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of why repeated image injection and resolution decoupling help, why low-resolution feature initialization may constrain later refinement, and why compact Gaussians accelerate fine-tuning. The principal limitations concerning self-attention scaling and required camera poses remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies two-view training on eight H100 GPUs for 200,000 iterations and documents wide-coverage preprocessing, hardware, and training resolutions. It removes explicit dataset counts, FPS/six-target-view sampling details, the VGG perceptual-feature disclosure, and the earlier high-resolution and 24-view fine-tuning budgets. These omissions change reproducibility information without establishing that the underlying procedures stopped.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to VGGT, FlashAttention-3, and Mip-Splatting, including a connection between its attention design and VGGT's alternating attention. It drops several references, including DINO, DINOv2, PointNet++, and VGG, and removes the statement associating GS-LRM/Long-LRM with pretrained 2D foundation models. Most research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: The document undergoes substantial structural reorganization: Related Works moves to Appendix A, quantitative and high-resolution discussions are consolidated, and architectural ablations are redistributed into Appendix E. Citation style changes throughout, and author information and acknowledgements are updated, although much method prose is retained.

P2.justification: v2 reformats the document, reorganizes tables, splits architectural ablations across displays, adds the wide-coverage table, and removes the runtime-scaling table. Main qualitative figures are consolidated on one page. Figures 6 and 10 lose the 11-view iLRM column, and Figures 9 and 10 each lose one scene example.

improvement.justification: The added matched-view DepthSplat comparisons, wide-coverage evaluation, and targeted component ablations provide stronger support for scalability and iterative refinement. The gain is tempered by removed runtime-scaling evidence and reproducibility details. Also, the new broad superiority claim over optimization-based methods needs qualification: Table 5 shows better PSNR and SSIM but worse LPIPS before fine-tuning. Overall, the empirical support improves, with material reporting limitations remaining.
